findings.claim: The `open-port-phases` change violates the path-ownership constraint by modifying `.kbd-orchestrator/project.json` phase metadata from a change.
findings.evidence: Constraints state: "`.kbd-orchestrator/project.json` — everything except `activePhase` | `/kbd-init` ONLY | Never written by a change." The `open-port-phases` proposal impact says: "`project.json` `phaseDefinitionOrder` grows by two," and its spec requires the new phases to appear in `prometheus kbd status --json` `phaseDefinitionOrder`.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not make an OpenSpec change write `phaseDefinitionOrder`; either route phase creation through the owning KBD skill outside the change, or revise the constraint through its owner before relying on this mutation.

findings.claim: The Docker CI task uses forbidden shell chaining, so the requested command is not portable under the project command policy.
findings.evidence: Constraints require: "No `&&`, `||` or `;` chaining — Windows PowerShell 5.1 rejects `&&`. Steps that must run in sequence are separate entries." `docker-services/tasks.md` task 5.2 says: "CI: `ci.yml` gains `docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml config` on all legs and `node scripts/services.mjs up && status && down` on `ubuntu-latest` only."
findings.suggested_fix: Specify separate CI steps or a Node wrapper for `up`, `status`, and `down`, with cleanup handled without shell chaining.

findings.claim: `pack-doctor` depends on a reusable `versions.toml` comparison library that `review-housekeeping` never creates.
findings.evidence: `pack-doctor/proposal.md` says `mini.versions-toml` "reuses `rules/test/versions-toml`'s comparison as a library function." But `review-housekeeping` only adds a test: "Add `rules/test/versions-toml.test.mjs`" and task 2.2 says to "Write `rules/test/versions-toml.test.mjs` first: parse with a minimal TOML reader..." with no library module or exported comparison API.
findings.suggested_fix: Have `review-housekeeping` create a non-test module, e.g. `rules/lib/versions-toml.mjs`, exporting the parser/comparison, and make both the test and doctor consume it.

findings.claim: `mini.sycophancy-correction` doctor check ownership is duplicated across two changes, risking duplicate IDs or conflicting implementations.
findings.evidence: `pack-doctor/proposal.md` includes the check in its initial set: "`mini.sycophancy-correction` (binary resolvable; degraded-not-failed)." Later, `sycophancy-correction-vendored/tasks.md` says: "write `lib/doctor/sycophancy.mjs`; register `mini.sycophancy-correction`." The `pack-doctor` change is ordered before `sycophancy-correction-vendored`.
findings.suggested_fix: Assign a single owner: either `pack-doctor` registers a placeholder check that later changes only enrich through injected dependencies, or `sycophancy-correction-vendored` alone adds and registers the check.

findings.claim: The OpenSpec fork tasks tell agents to use an SSH submodule URL, which is not a cross-platform or generally available checkout path for CI/users.
findings.evidence: `openspec-fork-submodule/tasks.md` task 1.1 says: "`git submodule add git@github.com:Prometheus-AGS/OpenSpec.git tools/openspec`". The proposal blocks clean checkout behavior on the submodule: "A clean checkout runs spec validation after install" and CI adds install before tests, but no SSH key availability is specified.
findings.suggested_fix: Use an HTTPS submodule URL unless there is an explicit project-wide SSH credential requirement and CI setup.
